Alex P.: Quick Q — returning from a 6mo international secondment on 2024-04-01. I want to switch my 401(k) deferral from pre-tax to Roth mid-quarter and also start catch-up contributions (turning 51 this year). Is that allowed immediately on my return? Also, my status changes to part-time on 2024-04-15 — how will that impact the employer HSA contribution proration? cc @Ryan Payroll

Katie HR: Welcome back in advance! Short answers: usually yes on deferral source changes (subject to payroll cutoff), catch-up should be allowed if you meet age rules, and HSA employer contributions are prorated when FTE changes mid-month/quarter depending on our vendor rules. Need a couple specifics from you.

Alex P.: Thanks. Specifics: last day before secondment was 2023-10-01, out until 2024-03-31, back 2024-04-01. Part-time = 0.6 FTE starting 2024-04-15. Would like Roth effective 2024-04-01 and catch-up started with first paycheck after return.

Ryan Payroll: Filing notes — payroll vendor processes 401(k) elective changes on cutoff dates. For monthly payroll our cutoff is the 20th prior to the pay period. If you want Roth effective 04-01 and into the 04 pay period, we need the change submitted by 2024-03-20. Catch-up (50+) is a separate flag on the deferral form and we can enable it the same effective date.

Alex P.: Ok will try to get form in by 03-20. For HSA: do we pro-rate the employer contribution for April because I go PT on 04-15? Or is it full month?

Katie HR: Our HSA employer contribution rule: if an employee's FTE changes within a month, vendor prorates contributions based on the pay-period FTE or a monthly FTE calculation depending on the plan year settings. For your case, because the change happens mid-pay-period (and the vendor uses monthly FTE), we expect a prorated April employer deposit. I can confirm exact dollar math with Ryan.

Ryan Payroll: Correct — vendor currently uses monthly FTE, so April = (days FT in month / total days) * full employer contribution. Because you were FT 1–14 and PT 15–30, April gets prorated. We'll send the calculation once we have the final FTE flag in payroll.

Ben T.: Tiny gotcha: if you change to Roth, your year-to-date pre-tax contributions still count for the annual pre-tax limit. Switching midyear doesn't re-characterize prior contributions. Make sure to watch annual limits across pre-tax + Roth (separate limit? — both count toward total deferral limit).

Alex P.: Good point Ben, I'm tracking. One more: any paperwork for the HSA employer contribution or is that automatic?

Katie HR: Employer side is automatic once payroll has your FTE change. But you need to opt in to HSA (if not already) and verify your HSA account info in the benefits portal. If you want employer deposit to a specific HSA custodian, confirm custodian in portal.

peopleops-bot: POLICY CLIP: 401(k) elective changes are subject to payroll vendor cutoff dates. Catch-up contributions (age 50+) may be enabled midyear upon request. HSA employer contributions are prorated for FTE changes within a month per vendor rules. For exceptions (manual adjustments), open a ticket to payroll@redwood.com with dates and self-reported amounts.

Ryan Payroll: Action items: @Alex P. — submit 401k elective change form with catch-up flag by 2024-03-20; confirm HSA custodian in benefits portal by 2024-03-25; notify if any retro pay needed. I'll queue the vendor ticket after your submission.

Alex P.: Will do. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

Katie HR: Ping me if Ryan flags anything, happy to help with forms.

Ben T.: FYI if you want, I can share a quick spreadsheet to project year-end tax impact switching to Roth midyear.

Alex P.: Yes please Ben — that'd be super helpful.

Ryan Payroll: Noting last msg at 1945678930 — closing the thread after forms submitted.
